risks: No human answers to the blocking ambiguities Q1 (60s p99 takedown bound) and Q2 (denylist ThreatCheck, fail open) reached this node; the plan is built on the model's proposed answers. If the business's published takedown number is sub-second, T11/T15/T17 change shape (synchronous multi-tier invalidation, no TTL safety net) and if a real reputation feed is expected, T18 is a materially larger task.

U4 is unresolved: Argon2PasswordEncoder references BouncyCastle but spring-security-crypto declares no such dependency. If T1 freezes the pom without an explicit bcprov-jdk18on pin, the code compiles and throws NoClassDefFoundError at the first sign-in (AC17), and neither implement nor author-tests may edit pom.xml to fix it.

U1 is unresolved: if the in-house Redis runs maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru, click counter keys can be evicted before T12's flush, silently losing clicks against AC3 with no error anywhere. Cluster mode additionally invalidates T19's Lua bucket unless every key is single-key or hash-tagged.

U5 is unresolved: a startup-generated JWT keypair makes a token issued by one instance unverifiable by another and invalidates sessions on restart, which breaks AC18's intent at more than one replica while passing every single-instance test.

T2 lowers app.cache.spec to <=60s in the same change that adds active invalidation (T15/T17). If the TTL is not lowered, a missed invalidation leaves a deleted or blocked link redirecting for up to five minutes, breaching the AC9 number quoted to fraud teams, and no gate detects it.

T11 replaces the body of CacheConfig.cacheManager rather than adding a second CacheManager bean. A parallel cache configuration class produces NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException and fails every class extending AbstractIntegrationTest at once, which reads like a broken harness rather than a bean conflict.

The first build of this run must be `./mvnw clean verify`: a stale service/target/classes/db/migration/V1__create_links.sql from an abandoned branch is on the classpath, is gitignored and invisible in review, and Flyway will apply it and then collide with T3's V1 under ddl-auto: validate.

T4 adds a second Testcontainer to a static-initialiser singleton pattern whose javadoc records a thirty-minute build caused by getting container lifecycle wrong; no redis image is in the local cache, so a cold pull inside a restricted network surfaces as a harness-wide timeout against verify's 5400s ceiling.

The routes_match_openapi gate only understands literal-string mappings; T11's root-level catch-all GET /{code} and any constant-valued path can fail the gate while the route is correct, and the redirect must not shadow /actuator/** or the reserved words in T10.

The no_secrets gate pattern fires on quoted credentials; T3's seeded customer fixture and T2's JWT key must use the existing unquoted ${VAR:default} env-placeholder style or the run halts on a false positive.

Coverage floor 0.70 is measured over a codebase several times the scaffold's size, and the branches least likely to be exercised by black-box HTTP tests are exactly T18's fail-open path, T19's over-limit path and T20's degraded mode; those need targeted tests, not incidental coverage.

docker-compose.yml is in no node's write paths and still defines Postgres only. Once the service needs Redis, `docker compose up` yields a service that cannot serve a click and no agent can fix it; it requires the human approving the T1 pom change to add the redis service in the same review.

Application configuration surface: Redis connection, JWT key placeholder and 24h TTL, rate-limit buckets, 30-day default expiry, public base URL, cache TTL <= 60s
V1 schema: customers, links (domain,code unique; status; expires_at), click totals, abuse reports, threat denylist, seeded customer fixture
Integration test harness with singleton Redis container alongside Postgres and a signed-in-session helper
JPA entities and repositories matching V1 exactly under ddl-auto: validate
Sign-in endpoint issuing an asymmetrically signed 24h JWT, with Argon2id/BCrypt password verification
Local-only session verification on /api/v1/** with the click path and actuator left unauthenticated
Unguessable short-code generator: 128-bit CSPRNG base62, no derivation from row/time/URL, unique-constraint retry
Create-link endpoint returning code and fully-qualified short URL, with URL validation, threat check and 30-day default expiry
Customer-chosen alias in the shared code namespace: charset and reserved-word rules, 409 on collision with no owner/target disclosure
Root redirect GET/HEAD /{code}: 302 with no-store headers, Redis-backed resolution cache with negative caching, identical 404 for unknown/expired/deleted/blocked, 405 otherwise
Exact click counting: Redis increment on the hot path, batched durable flush to PostgreSQL, no counting of 404s
Owner-scoped link performance endpoint returning PostgreSQL total plus un-flushed Redis delta, 404 for links that are not yours
Owner-scoped paginated list of a customer's own links
Owner-scoped soft delete with active cache invalidation, verified to stop redirecting inside the 60s bound
Owner-scoped expiry-only PATCH on a link, with the target URL immutable and cache invalidation on change
Authenticated, rate-limited abuse report that blocks the link immediately and records reporter id and timestamp
ThreatCheck port with Postgres denylist and no-op implementations, failing open with a log line when unavailable
Redis token-bucket rate limiting: per-IP click bucket, tighter 404/enumeration bucket, per-customer write bucket, 429 with Retry-After
Degraded-mode behaviour: clicks served and counted best-effort when Redis or the create path's dependencies are down, health reports the truth
Acceptance suite pinning the cross-cutting guarantees: takedown bound, 404 indistinguishability, code unguessability, counting exactness under repeat clicks, hot-link spike
Design docs reconciled with the frozen assumptions so reviewers are not reading superseded decisions
